findings.claim: The independent Lyapunov route (positive definite P) agrees with the numpy eigenvalue route on every route-family plant

hypothesis: The PLSR matrix route (Lyapunov solve, then the sign of max eig of the decrease form beyond the resolution) agrees with independent references -- numpy eigenvalues and SciPy's Bartels-Stewart Lyapunov solvers -- while the scalar quadratic route (the sign of x^T M x at sampled states) cannot certify definiteness and misses thin positive cones.
input_data: 30 continuous plants n = 2..5 (PCG64 seed 111) with |spectral abscissa| > 0.05
Thin-cone plant A = diag(-0.5, 5e-7), P = I (decrease form diag(-1, 1e-6)) with 64 random unit states (seed 1111)
mathematical_model: Rayleigh: x^T M x <= max eig(M) |x|^2 for every x, with equality only on the top eigenvector, so sampled negativity never implies negative definiteness. An unstable A has v*(A + A^T)v = 2 Re(lambda)|v|^2 > 0 for an eigenvector v, so P = I can never certify it. For n = 1 the decrease form is 2 a p (continuous), so the verdict must follow sign(a) whenever 2|a|p exceeds the resolution.
numerical_result: Solver agreement: max relative difference 1.73e-14 over 15 continuous and 4.50e-16 over 15 discrete PLSR solves (scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_lyapunov@1.16.2; scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_lyapunov@1.16.2). solve_lyapunov: 0 disagreements with numpy stability over 50 plants, 20 refusals (20 of them numpy-unstable plants). Verdicts: 0 stable plants not certified with their own P, 0 unstable plants certified with P = I. Thin cone: 64/64 sampled scalar decreases negative; PLSR codes {'DECREASE_NOT_DEFINITE': 64}. Scalar plants: {'-1': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-1e-10': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-1e-300': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-4.94066e-324': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '0': 'NUMERICAL_INCONCLUSIVE', '4.94066e-324': 'NOT_CERTIFIED', '1e-300': 'NOT_CERTIFIED', '1': 'NOT_CERTIFIED'}. Conclusion: the matrix routes agree with each other on margin-separated plants; sampled scalar decrease cannot stand in for them.
observation_model: PLSR solve_lyapunov outcome (P or refusal) and verdicts with the returned P and with P = I; SciPy (or the CIW Kronecker solve when SciPy is absent) Lyapunov P per time convention; numpy eigenvalues; PLSR verdicts at 64 sampled states.

title: Compare scalar quadratic and matrix-eigenvalue routes.
uncertainty: Solver differences are at rounding level; route agreement holds only with the stated stability margins. The subnormal scalar entries are reported, not asserted.
unresolved_assumptions: Plants with margins below 0.05 are excluded, so the comparison says nothing about near-marginal plants (T107 covers those).
The independent solver is SciPy when installed, otherwise the CIW Kronecker solve (same Lyapunov equation, different code).
